A moon can be harrow-sworn to two differ.why: "Harrow-sworn" is a made-up relation (catalogued as harrow_sworn_to, fictional, no property tags): it does not occur in Dolma or on Wikipedia, and its words carry no default reading about how many planets a moon can be tied to. A made-up relation has no property to contradict.

notes: RBox expansion paired with physics-replace-0012 (which makes 'directly orbits' not functional): a made-up relation, harrow_sworn_to, is given the same property, not functional, applied to real moons and planets. The relation is deliberately not an orbit word ('gyre' or 'circles' would let the model answer from real orbital knowledge): each moon here really orbits one planet, so a model that read the relation as orbiting would answer 'rules it out' without the edit, and only the edit gives 'no'. The direct question and first instance ask whether a second tie is excluded (no); the second asks whether it could hold (yes). The negation is worded as the plain opposite of the edit (cannot be harrow-sworn to two); its answer is no. Side facts and unrelated queries are those of the revision record.
